title: Inline PERFORM headers and EXIT PERFORM read as PERFORM targets
shapes: PERFORM WS-N TIMES ... END-PERFORM (inline, identifier count)
PERFORM 3100-FORMAT-TOTAL 2 TIMES (out-of-line: a real edge, the control case)
asserts: An inline PERFORM names no procedure, so it draws no edge; EXIT PERFORM is not a PERFORM. Out-of-line PERFORM procedure-name n TIMES is an edge to the procedure.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: The PERFORM statement is an out-of-line PERFORM statement, when procedure-name-1 is specified. ... The PERFORM statement is an inline PERFORM statement, when procedure-name-1 is omitted.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: The EXIT statement ... provides a way to exit from a section, a paragraph, or an inline PERFORM statement.

notes: PERFORM FOREVER (#4305's GnuCOBOL / Micro Focus form) is not planted: it is not Enterprise COBOL, and this estate is IBM dialect. Its IBM counterpart, PERFORM UNTIL EXIT, is a phase-1 candidate.
